neighbours.label: a bad event framed as an isolated exception to an otherwise good norm (an exception, an aberration, a fluke, a one-off), as opposed to the same event framed as typical
fire: The flight was delayed, but I think that was an exception for an airline that is usually punctual.
The coach called the heavy defeat an aberration in an otherwise brilliant season.
Scientists said the warm February was likely a fluke rather than a new trend.
The manager assured us the rude waiter was an exception and not how staff behave.
Fans hope the early exit was a one-off and that the team will bounce back.
The mayor described the riot as an aberration in a famously peaceful town.
My laptop crashed once last year, but it seems that was just a fluke.
The cold room was an exception; every other night at the inn was perfect.
quiet: The flight was delayed, which is normal for an airline that is never punctual.
The coach called the heavy defeat typical of a team that has struggled all season.
Scientists said the warm February fits a long trend of rising temperatures.
The manager admitted that rude waiters are how his staff usually behave.
Fans fear the early exit reflects deeper problems in the team.
The mayor described the riot as the latest in a long series of clashes.
If the file is missing, the function raises an exception and stops.
The cold room was like every other night at the inn: uncomfortable.

predictions: exception framings 0.4-1.0; typical framings and programming 'exception' below 0.25
notes: Card: ' exception', aberr|ation, fl|uke, 'a handful of', 'simply a case of', promotes isolated/anomaly/temporary/outlier.
